papers.title: Tight lower bounds for Lipschitz geodesically convex optimization on hyperbolic space
papers.abstract: We determine the dimension-independent first-order query complexity of minimizing a Lipschitz geodesically convex (g-convex) function on hyperbolic space. Given a ball of radius $r$ containing a global minimizer, we prove that $\Omega(\zeta_r/\epsilon^2)$ queries are necessary to attain accuracy $\epsilon Mr$, where $M$ is the Lipschitz constant and $\zeta_r=r/\tanh r$ captures the effect of curvature. This matches the known $O(\zeta_r/\epsilon^2)$ upper bound for the Riemannian subgradient method (Zhang and Sra, 2016). This is the first query-complexity result for g-convex optimization that is tight simultaneously in curvature and target accuracy. The standard Euclidean recipe of constructing hard instances as maxima of affine functions does not transfer to hyperbolic space, so the lower bound requires a new mechanism. Our starting point is the worst-function construction of Criscitiello and Boumal (2023, Appendix A). It gives the same lower bound for a subclass of algorithms, including the subgradient method, whose queries remain in prescribed g-convex regions. We retain this geometric setup and carefully tune and augment their hard function to accommodate every deterministic first-order algorithm. The key new mechanism is an advance-or-stall scheme: when a query lies in these regions, the oracle reveals at most one new information direction (advance); when a query leaves them, we show that the oracle can answer without revealing any new hidden direction (stall). Unlike earlier curvature-dependent lower bounds, the proof uses no ball-packing argument.

papers.title: Geodesics in the Deep Linear Network
papers.abstract: We derive a general system of ordinary differential equations and associated explicit solutions in a special case for geodesics between full rank matrices in the deep linear network geometry. In the process, we find horizontal straight lines in the invariant balanced manifold that remain geodesics under Riemannian submersion.

papers.title: Variational mean curvatures for general $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ domains
papers.abstract: The notion of variational mean curvature (VMC) arises from Massari's variational approach to hypersurfaces of prescribed mean curvature and expresses a minimizing property for Massari's functional. Here, we complement the theory of VMCs with a new sharp relation between hypersurface regularity and VMC integrability. In fact, our main result asserts that every bounded open set in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ boundary, $0<\alpha<1$, has a global VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for every $p<\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}$. In addition, we underpin sharpness of this conclusion by constructing examples of bounded open sets in $\mathbb{R}^n$ with $\mathrm{C}^{1,\alpha}$ boundary which do not admit a VMC in $\mathrm{L}^p(\mathbb{R}^n)$ for any $p>\frac{1+\alpha}{1-\alpha}$. Our proofs are based on Barozzi's level-set construction of global VMCs and determine integrability of these VMCs by geometric investigation of their superlevel sets and of related unions of balls.

papers.title: Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation in higher dimensions II
papers.abstract: This is the second of two papers on isolated singularities of positive solutions to the Yamabe equation on manifolds with nonflat background metrics. In the first paper, we proved that, in dimensions $3\le n\le29$, every isolated singularity is either removable or the solution is asymptotic to a radial model singular solution in the flat metric on the Euclidean space with origin as its singular point---a Fowler solution. In the present paper, we show that this dimension range is sharp. More precisely, for each $n\ge30$, we construct a smooth metric on $\mathbb{RP}^n$ and a positive solution of the corresponding Yamabe equation having an isolated singularity, near which the solution blows up along a sequence at a rate much faster than that of Fowler solutions. Moreover, the singular solution defines a complete conformal metric of constant positive scalar curvature and the metric agrees with the round metric to infinite order at the singular point.

papers.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
papers.abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.

papers.title: On solutions to tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations
papers.abstract: This paper develops convex analysis on tropical varieties and investigates the properties of the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. We start by introducing notions of plurisubharmonic functions and K\"ahler forms on arbitrary tropical varieties. We show that many classical results of pluripotential theory extend to this setting, including an analogue of Demailly's regularization theorem. Next, we study the solutions to the tropical Monge-Amp\`ere equations. While we establish their uniqueness, we show that the existence is not guaranteed in general. More precisely, we prove that the tropical analogue of the Calabi-Yau theorem fails for any pair $(X, \theta)$ consisting of a compact tropical variety $X$ of dimension at least two satisfying a mild genericity assumption, and a tropical K\"ahler form $\theta$ on $X$. In particular, there exist measures compactly supported in the open part of $X$ that admit no solution. In contrast, for tropical varieties that are regular in codimension one, we show the existence of solutions. Finally, via strongly faithful tropicalizations whose existence is established in this paper, we relate the tropical solutions, when they exist, to the solutions of non-Archimedean Monge-Amp\`ere equations on Berkovich spaces.

papers.title: The Eighth-Order Evolution Model for Closed Planar Curves
papers.abstract: We consider the $L^2(ds)$ gradient flow of $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$ for smooth closed immersed planar curves. The stationary curves are precisely the multiply covered circles. We give an explicit sufficient condition under which the elastic energy is non-increasing and for each nonzero turning number, explicit small initial scale-invariant energy yields a global smooth solution with bounded positive length and exponential convergence to a fixed multiply covered circle, after reparametrisation. We note that that the qualitative rigidity and convergence results are already contained in the generalised ideal flow theory of McCoy and Wheeler. The present paper gives quantitative measure of small initial data, corrected evolution identities, and a complete argument in the case of the curvature energy $\frac12\int k_{ss}^2\,ds$.

papers.title: A new localization approach for Willmore flows: Asymptotic analysis for the Dirichlet problem
papers.abstract: We study the Willmore flow with Dirichlet boundary conditions by means of a new geometric localization approach. In contrast to previous works, we do not rely on localized energy estimates, but on uniformly controlled isothermal coordinates and localized parabolic a priori estimates. For genus-zero surfaces satisfying an explicit energy condition depending only on the prescribed boundary data, we prove global existence together with a dichotomy between smooth convergence and subconvergence to a complete noncompact Willmore surface. If the initial Willmore energy is at most $4\pi$, this dichotomy reduces to smooth convergence after reparametrization, and we show that this additional threshold is optimal. As an application, we obtain an existence criterion for the stationary Dirichlet Willmore problem.

papers.title: Split Normal Bundles and Rigidity of Holomorphic Immersions from Compact Ball Quotients
papers.abstract: Let $f$ be a holomorphic immersion from a compact complex hyperbolic space form into a higher-dimensional complex hyperbolic space form. We prove that if the normal bundle decomposes as a direct sum of holomorphic line bundles, then the immersion is totally geodesic. This result has no restriction on the codimension and extends, under the splitting hypothesis, the classical rigidity theorem of Cao--Mok. The proof uses the polarized complex variation of Hodge structure induced from the target. The line-bundle decomposition produces nef zero-Higgs line quotients, and a Chern-character identity forces the Gauss-defect form to have nontrivial nullity at every point. The null-foliation and boundary argument of Cao--Mok then shows that the defect vanishes identically. In particular, this answers a question posed by Mok almost twenty years ago about decomposable normal bundles for complex surfaces immersed in four-dimensional complex hyperbolic space forms.

papers.title: A counterexample to the local existence of conformal normal metrics
papers.abstract: For every dimension $n\ge3$, we construct a smooth Riemannian metric whose entire Taylor series at a point agrees with the Euclidean metric and whose conformal class contains no smooth conformal normal metric near that point. For the metric used in the construction, parametrized by a smooth angular function, we prove that conformal normalization forces a dimension-dependent exponential decay rate for the spherical harmonic components of that function. This gives counterexamples whenever the angular coefficients decay too slowly. In particular, every nonanalytic angular function yields a counterexample. The proof combines a weighted cylinder estimate with an integral identity relating the angular spectral coefficients of the background volume defect to the nonlinear remainder. We also give a direct counterexample to the linear right inverse used in Cao's smooth existence argument and identify the failure of angular summability in that construction.

papers.title: K\"ahler-Ricci Flow is Symplectic Deflation plus an Exact Symplectic Deformation
papers.abstract: We demonstrate that K\"ahler-Ricci flow on a Fano surface decomposes as a symplectic deflation along a plurianticanonical divisor plus an exact symplectic deformation in the divisor complement. We apply this decomposition to the study of certain projective bundles. We establish the optimal decay rate in the setting of Song, Sz\'ekelyhidi, and Weinkove for a family of toric metrics which match the cohomological profile of K\"ahler-Ricci flow. In doing so, we identify a $C^2$-obstruction to proving the optimal decay rate in the setting of ruled toric surfaces. We present these ideas as a new symplectic-topological approach to the study of K\"ahler-Ricci flow.

papers.title: Index-one capillary minimal hypersurfaces in \(\mathbb R^n_+\)
papers.abstract: We classify complete, two-sided, properly embedded capillary minimal surfaces with nonempty boundary and Morse index one in \(\mathbb R^3_+\). More precisely, if the boundary is compact, these surfaces are catenoid truncations; if the boundary is noncompact, they are capillary hairpin surfaces. The classification extends to higher dimensions under extrinsic Euclidean volume growth and Wang--Zhang's dimension and angle conditions.

papers.title: Pseudodifferential structure, rigidity, and sharpness for the Steklov problem on differential forms
papers.abstract: We resolve four questions concerning Karpukhin's Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator on differential forms. First, for $0\leq p\leq n-2$, we prove that the operator is classical pseudodifferential of order one and compute its principal symbol, which is elliptic on the coclosed symbol space. This answers Open Question 7.19 in the survey of Colbois, Girouard, Gordon, and Sher [7]. Second, the symbol calculation yields a Weyl law with remainder $O(\tau^{n-2})$, resolving the smooth case of their Open Question 7.23 in [7]. Third, in the critical dimension $n=2p+2$, we show that conformal deformations of the Euclidean ball fixing the boundary metric preserve the full operator. Nonisometric metrics therefore retain all equalities in Karpukhin's initial equality range, disproving the isometry-rigidity assertion of Conjecture 2.12 in [19](the rigidity assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]). Fourth, we establish the all-index sharpness asserted in Conjecture 2.13 in [19](the sharpness assertion of Conjecture 7.27 in [7]) in the class of smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian manifolds with boundary. For $p\geq1$, a shrinking-core construction inspired by the collapsing models of Ann\'e and Takahashi produces manifolds with fixed spherical boundary and explicit two-sided bounds for an initial eigenvalue cluster.

papers.title: Semi-classical Szeg\H{o} kernel asymptotics on CR manifolds of high codimension
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a CR manifold $X$ of high codimension and a CR line bundle $L$ over $X$. For each $k \in \mathbb{N}$, let $L^k$ denote the $k$-th power of $L$. We establish that the spectral projection $\Pi_{k,\leq k\mu_k} := \mathbf{1}_{(-\infty, k\mu_k]}(\Box_{b,k})$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions, where $\Box_{b,k}$ denotes the Kohn Laplacian with values in $L^k$. Moreover, when $\Box_{b,k}$ possesses a local spectral gap, we show that the Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_k$ converges to the weighted Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the sense of distributions. We also provide an explicit formula for the Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group. Furthermore, we consider a high codimension CR manifold $X$ equipped with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action. In this setting, we prove that the partial Szeg\H{o} projection $\Pi_{k,({\mathbb R}^m\curvearrowright,\leq k\delta)}$ converges to the weighted partial Szeg\H{o} projection on the high codimension Heisenberg group in the $\mathcal{C}^\infty$ topology. As an application of our results, we establish a Kodaira embedding theorem for high codimension CR manifolds with a transversal and CR $\mathbb{R}^m$-action.

papers.title: Endpoint capacity at strictly stable minimal boundaries:Gaussian layers and Schwarzschild deficits
papers.abstract: Let $(M^n,\mathfrak g)$, $3\le n\le7$, be a one-ended asymptotically flat manifold whose boundary $\Sigma$ is a connected, strictly stable, outermost minimal hypersurface. As $p\downarrow1$, the $p$-capacity of $\Sigma$ converges to its area, by a theorem of Fogagnolo and Mazzieri. We establish a higher-order asymptotic expansion governed by a single function on $\Sigma$: the positive solution $g$ of the reciprocal Jacobi equation $Jg=g^{-1}$. After a universal term, the first correction is determined by the average of $\log g$, and the capacitary potential drops from one to zero across a Gaussian boundary layer of width $g\sqrt{p-1}$; under the normalized energy measure, the logarithm of the gradient has limiting variance $\frac12$ plus the variance of $\log g$. In dimension three, assuming in addition that $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\ge0$ along $\Sigma$, we identify the capacity deficit of $\Sigma$ relative to the Schwarzschild horizon of the same area at order $p-1$: it is nonnegative, vanishes exactly when the induced metric of $\Sigma$ is round and $R_{\mathfrak g}+|\mathrm{II}|^2\equiv0$, and controls the deviation of $g$ from a constant through a relative-entropy identity.

papers.title: Tensorial pinching by deforming curvature cones in higher codimension mean curvature flow
papers.abstract: We develop a pinching method for mean curvature flow in higher codimension. Motivated by pinching constructions for Ricci flow, the method uses a nonlinear deformation of the second fundamental form. We introduce two tensorial curvature conditions for closed immersions in Euclidean space which extend beyond the scope of classical scalar pinching results. In dimensions at least ten, we apply the method to prove convergence to a round point under the first condition and a canonical neighborhood theorem under the second.

papers.title: Quantitative stratification and optimal regularity for stationary $J$-holomorphic maps
papers.abstract: In this paper, we give an alternate proof of the $\epsilon$-regularity theorem of Wang [Comm. Cont. Math. 2003] for weakly $J$-holomorphic maps by adapting the conservation law approach of Rivi\`ere [Invent. Math. 2007]. Then we adapt the powerful quantitative stratification method of Naber--Valtorta [Ann. Math. 2017] to obtain optimal volume estimates and rectifiability for the quantitative strata of stationary $J$-holomorphic maps. In contrast with general harmonic maps, the almost complex equation gives rise to an additional symmetry improvement: Every odd-dimensional translation symmetry extends to an even-dimensional one. Consequently, consecutive even and odd strata coincide, and the $k$-th quantitative stratum satisfies a tubular-neighborhood estimate with exponent $2m-2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$, where $2m$ is the real dimension of the domain. The corresponding strata are $2\lfloor k/2\rfloor$-rectifiable, with almost-everywhere unique complex planes of symmetry. Finally, we prove that every stationary $J$-holomorphic map is smooth if the target { manifold} admits no non-constant $J$-holomorphic sphere, improving the corresponding theorem of Wang.

papers.title: Quadratic growth rigidity for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation
papers.abstract: For the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation on $\mathbb{C}^{n}$, we prove the Liouville theorem for solutions with quadratic growth.

papers.title: Outer trapped surface formation from gravitational waves collision
papers.abstract: We give a new rigorous construction of outer trapped surface formation in smooth vacuum spacetimes without symmetry assumptions. The outer trapped surface is produced by the collision of two transversely localized, nearly plane-fronted gravitational waves described by short pulse data. The outer trapped surface is obtained by joining two smooth pieces along a curve with their future-directed outer null normals matching continuously. The incompleteness of the maximal future development is then established by adapting Penrose's original argument. This construction is inspired by Penrose's argument in constructing a marginally outer trapped surface in the collision of two ultra-relativistic particles modeled by the Aichelburg--Sexl solution.

papers.title: Sharp Quartic Pinching for the Mean Curvature Flow in the Sphere
papers.abstract: We prove a sharp quartic curvature pinching for the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$, $m\ge2$, which generalises Pu's work on the convergence of submanifolds in $\mathbb{S}^{n+m}$ to a round point. Using a blow up argument, we prove a codimension and a cylindrical estimate, where in regions of high curvature, the submanifold becomes approximately codimension one, quantitatively, and is weakly convex and moves by translation or is a self shrinker. With a decay estimate, the rescaling converges smoothly to a totally geodesic limit in infinite time, without using Stampacchia iteration or integral analysis.

papers.title: A new look at unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction for toric manifolds
papers.abstract: For a symplectic manifold $M$ with the Hamiltonian action of a compact Lie group $G$, we give a new perspective on the problem of unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence. We argue that this correspondence leads naturally to the introduction of what we call Fourier polarizations, whose real directions include the Hamiltonian vector fields of all invariant functions of the moment map. For a Fourier polarization, quantization commutes with reduction unitarily. For a general $G$-invariant polarization, $\mathcal{P}$, unitarity in the quantization commutes with reduction correspondence can then be formulated in terms of the existence of a Fourier polarization, $\mathcal{P}_F$, such that the quantizations with respect to $\mathcal{P}$ and to $\mathcal{P}_F$ are unitarily equivalent. We describe this perspective in detail for symplectic toric manifolds, by considering symplectic reductions associated to the action of a subtorus $T^p\subset T^n$. We consider half-form quantization in Fourier (mixed) polarizations $\mathcal{P}_\infty$, whose real directions are generated by(the Hamiltonian vector fields of the)components of the $T^p$ moment map. We show that Fourier mixed polarizations of this type can be obtained by Mabuchi geodesic rays of toric K\"ahler structures, starting at a given initial structure and with velocity given by the norm square of the moment map of the torus subgroup. We lift these geodesic rays to the quantum bundle via generalized coherent state transforms, which define equivariant isomorphisms between quantum Hilbert spaces for the K\"ahler and Fourier polarizations, where the later are obtained at infinite geodesic time. Unitarity in quantization commutes with reduction in these cases then becomes equivalent to the unitarity of these isomorphisms. In general, however, in the toric case, these isomorphisms are not unitary.

papers.title: Levi Flat Structures via Structure Sheaves: Differential Complexes, Convexity, and Global Solvability
papers.abstract: This paper investigates Levi flat structures from the perspective of structure sheaves. We employ formal integrability to construct a class of differential complexes, thereby providing a resolution of the structure sheaf and a global realization of the Treves complex. Drawing inspiration from Morse theory and Grauert's convexity, we introduce notions of convexity and positivity that fully exploit Levi flatness, which yield global exactness of the differential complex and Sobolev regularity in the compact case. As applications, we establish the global solvability of the Treves complex for Levi flat structures, together with results on singular cohomology and the extension problem for canonical forms in the elliptic case.

papers.title: Envelope of Holomorphy of Matsuki Orbits in Complex Grassmannians
papers.abstract: We study the envelopes of holomorphy of Matsuki orbits $M_{\ell,m,r}$ arising as intersections of $G_0$- and $K$-orbits in complex Grassmannians. These orbits, equipped with natural CR-structures, form a class of compact homogeneous CR-submanifolds whose analytic continuation properties are of fundamental interest. Building on Rossi's theory of holomorphic extension, we establish that the envelope of holomorphy of each Matsuki orbit coincides biholomorphically with the containing $K$-orbit $O_{\ell,m}$. Our approach provides a geometric proof based on the holomorphic fiber bundle structure $\pi : M_{\ell,m,r} \to \mathrm{Gr}_{\ell}(E_+) \times \mathrm{Gr}_{m}(E_-)$, clarifying the role of compact isotropic fibers in constraining holomorphic extension. Explicit examples, including the orbit $M_{1,1,1} \subset \mathrm{Gr}_3(\mathbb{C}^8)$, illustrate the method and highlight connections with classical constructions in complex geometry and representation theory.

papers.title: Ancient Gauss curvature flows of bounded width
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct a pancake-like ancient compact solution with flat sides to the Gauss curvature flow, contained in a slab. Also, we construct sausage-like ancient compact solutions to the $\alpha$-Gauss curvature flow with $\alpha >\frac{1}{2}$, asymptotic to a round cylinder.

papers.title: Distance Functions, Curvature and Topology
papers.abstract: We discuss some properties of the distance functions on Riemannian manifolds and we relate their behavior to the geometry of the manifolds. This leads to alternative proofs of some "classical" theorems connecting curvature and topology.

papers.title: Recovering a Riemannian manifold from minimal surface areas
papers.abstract: We study the recovery of a three-dimensional Riemannian manifold from the areas of minimal surfaces. We show that areas of minimal surfaces determine the metric on manifolds foliated by minimal surfaces, up to boundary-fixing isometry. This resolves the conjecture on boundary rigidity for least-area data in an exterior formulation, even without topological restrictions on the minimal surfaces. We also prove global rigidity for Einstein metrics on compact three-manifolds with boundary, assuming $\(\pi_1(M,\partial M)=0\)$ and a non-trapping condition. The Einstein result includes the

papers.title: An equiregular counterexample to the Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps
papers.abstract: Lerario, Rizzi and Tiberio disproved the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture with a rank-two distribution on $\mathbb R^4$, of degree of nonholonomy five at the origin, whose endpoint map from that point has no regular values. Their distribution is neither equiregular nor real-analytic, and the equiregular case has remained open. We construct an equiregular rank-two distribution on an open set diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^9$, with small growth vector $(2,3,5,8,9)$, whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values. This growth vector is maximal and generic for rank-two distributions in dimension nine, so the failure of the Sard property is not tied to any degeneracy of the growth vector. Singular curves of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio-type structure built from the same coefficient lift, inside the strip where our distribution is defined, to singular curves, and the vertical displacement of a horizontal loop is an explicit strip integral. Realising an open set of vertical displacements by singular loops reduces to a graded moment problem, which we solve with pairs of bumps of opposite winding, an anisotropic rescaling, and an inverse function theorem uniform over infinitely many scales. We also state, with proofs deferred to a planned longer version, two results about our distribution: a description of its abnormal dynamics in the cotangent bundle, which explains the example from a dynamical point of view, and the non-constancy of its Tanaka symbol. The latter motivates an equiregular counterexample in dimension twelve with constant Tanaka symbol (constant nilpotentisation), announced here and to be proved in a separate paper. The longer version will also contain obstructions to real-analytic and lower-dimensional versions, and a transversal variant of the construction, which also leads to a modification of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio counterexample.

papers.title: Inhomogeneous balanced non-K\"ahler metrics on complex projective spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the cohomogeneity one action of $G_{p,q}=\mathrm{U}(p+1)\times\mathrm{U}(q+1)$ on $\mathbb{C}P^{p+q+1}$, where $p\geq q\geq 1$ and $p>1$. We characterize all $G_{p,q}$-invariant Riemannian metrics compatible with the canonical complex structure and obtain parametrizations of the invariant K\"ahler and balanced metrics. As an application, we use these parametrizations to construct a family of inhomogeneous balanced non-K\"ahler metrics with positive scalar curvature on complex projective spaces of odd complex dimension.

papers.title: Arithmetic Constraints on Charges of Symmetric Monopoles
papers.abstract: For Euclidean BPS monopoles with gauge group $SU(N)$, maximal symmetry breaking, and sufficiently generic spectral data, we produce necessary congruence relations that their magnetic charges must satisfy when $N \geq 3$. As such, a monopole as above with given charges can have certain subgroups of $SO(3)$ ruled out as possible groups of symmetries. In particular, the axially symmetric case may only admit non-trivial magnetic charges in the non-generic setting.

papers.title: Tetrahedral points and classification of Almgren-minimizing sets in $\mathbb{R}^3$
papers.abstract: We prove that a two-dimensional Almgren-minimizing set in three dimensions which is sufficiently close in Hausdorff distance to a tetrahedral cone contains an interior tetrahedral point. As a consequence, we obtain quantitative regularity near tetrahedral cones and we complete the classification of entire Almgren-minimizers in $\mathbb{R}^3$.
